The nanowires were grown by molecular beam epitaxy using the vapor-liquid-solid growth mode with gold catalyst particles on a GaAs(111)B substrate.
The (In,Ga)As core nanowires were grown at a high temperature of around 500°C, while the (Ga,Mn)As shells were deposited at a much lower temperature of 220°C.
The (In,Ga)As core nanowires have a diameter of 70-100 nm and a length of up to 1.6 micrometers.
The nominal indium content in the (In,Ga)As core is around 13%, but the actual concentration is likely lower at around 10%.
The (Ga,Mn)As shell has a thickness of around 12 nanometers and a manganese content of approximately 5%.
High-resolution transmission electron microscopy and Raman scattering measurements confirm that both the (In,Ga)As core and (Ga,Mn)As shell have a wurtzite crystal structure.
The (Ga,Mn)As shell exhibits ferromagnetic coupling at temperatures above 33 K, but the overall magnetic behavior is superparamagnetic due to the material being in a blocked state below around 17 K.

The growth of the (Ga,Mn)As shell at low temperature (220°C) is crucial for achieving the high manganese content necessary for ferromagnetism, as higher growth temperatures limit the manganese incorporation.
The growth rate of the (In,Ga)As nanowires is about 5 times faster than the growth rate of planar (In,Ga)As layers under the same flux conditions.
A (Ga,Mn)As layer also grows in between the nanowires during the shell deposition, with a thickness of up to 70 nm.

Magnetic measurements on the nanowires were performed after transferring them to a diamagnetic substrate to separate the nanowire signal from the magnetic contributions of the original substrate and other contaminants.
The absence of the GaAs-like LO phonon mode in the Raman spectra indicates the high quality of the (In,Ga)As nanowire cores, with minimal structural defects.
The shift in the TO phonon mode frequency in the Raman spectra is used to estimate the indium content in the (In,Ga)As cores as around 12 ± 4%.

The presence of a shoulder in the Raman spectra at 274.5 cm^-1 is attributed to a hole-concentration-induced coupled plasmon-LO-phonon mode, indicating a hole concentration of around 3x10^19 cm^-3 in the (Ga,Mn)As shell.
The wurtzite crystal structure of the nanowires is different from the typical zinc-blende structure observed in planar layers of these materials, opening up new possibilities for device applications.
